newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico stocks stage sharp late recovery on Dow.
newsitem.headline: Mexico stocks stage sharp late recovery on Dow.

text.p: Mexican blue chips turned around sharply in late trade to end sharply up on Monday after slumping for most of the session in parallel with Wall Street, traders said.
"It was nothing other than the Dow (Jones) and dealers took advantage of (cheap) prices to buy ahead of first quarter earnings reports," a floor trader said.
The leading IPC share index ended up 34.19 points, or 0.91 percent, at 3,798.65 after sliding as low as 3,707.65 at mid-afternoon trade.
Trading volume also recovered from being in the doldrums for most of the day to close at 89.97 million shares, or more than for many recent sessions.
"Dealers settled a lot of in-and-out trades at the close, which is why the bourse rebounded, although it had a hard time doing so than the Dow," another trader said.
The Dow Jones, meanwhile, closed up 60.21 points at 6,451.90 points.
Analysts drew attention to the fact the IPC rebounded at just above a psychological barrier at 3,700 points.

"It was very important the IPC stayed above the 3,700 point mark. Despite our recent falls, returns on the bourse for the year to date are still in positive turf, as opposed to Wall Street," said Esteban Rojas, an analyst with the Arka brokerage in Mexico City.
Rojas was cautious, however, regarding reaction on the bourse to forthcoming key U.S. economic data and whether they augured further interest rate hikes to curb overheating. "We
have U.S. consumer prices, industrial output and trade balance figures in the coming days, all of which are important for determining the strength of the U.S. economy," he said.
Expected increases in domestic interest rates at Tuesday's primary auction could also pour cold water on the prospect of Monday's gain in stock prices continuing, traders said.
"I feel the bourse will continue to be volatile, we expect hikes in Cetes rates. Foreign brokers we saw in the market are awaiting the outcome (of the auction)," a desk trader said.
Money market traders said they forecast increases of up to 100 basis points in bellwether 28-day Cetes rates at Banco de Mexico's weekly auction of government securities on Tuesday.
Traders said a late rebound by telecomms firm Telmex weighed most on the bourse's late recovery.
Telmex L shares ended up 22 centavos at 16.06 pesos, up from a session low of 15.70 pesos. Telmex ADRs meanwhile ended unchanged at 40, but after recovering from a low of 39-5/8.
Traders and analyst noted that key financial and construction stocks declined sharply on expectations they would post poor first quarter earnings.
Construction firm Tribasa ended down 1.20 pesos at 23.50 pesos. Financial stock GFB B shares fell 11 centavos to 2.47 pesos, while counterparts Serfin A shares closed down 1.20 pesos to 23.50 pesos.
The broad market did not match the late upswing in blue chips and ended mixed. Of a total of 108 stocks traded, declines outnumbered gains by 47 to 31.

"Leading gainers .PG.MX were not very representative and and decliners .PL.MX just fell on profit-taking. The only decliner which slid for some other reason was Serfin, which they are probably selling off because they expect a poor earnings report," a trader said.
(( --Karina Balderas, Mexico City newsroom +525 728-9562))
